newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel calls for $7 bln EPA 1998 budget.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel calls for $7 bln EPA 1998 budget.

text.p: The U.S. Senate subcommittee in charge of the Environmental Protection Agency's budget recommended the agency should have $6.98 billion to spend in the 1998 fiscal year.

The total was $180 million more than Congress approved for 1997, but was $670 million less than the Clinton administration sought, mainly because the panel refused to support a 50 percent increase in spending on toxic waste cleanups before Congress overhauled the Superfund program.
The Senate panel voted to provide $1.4 billion for Superfund cleanups, almost unchanged from this year, and $600 million less than the administration requested.

However, with an eye to aiding local governments, and with bipartisan support, the panel voted to restore $275 million for a total of $1.35 billion in funding for clean water loans to communities and full funding for cleaning up abandoned former industrial sites.
The spending bill also included $725 million for the federal safe drinking water loan fund, which matched the administration's request and provided $175 million more than in 1997.
The Senate panel's total EPA spending recommendation was $250 million less than the House Appropriations committee approved last week.
